title: First Principles of Tennis: developmental pathway
opening: A missed ball does not tell you by itself what to practice. Check the point, test one possible cause, then return to play.

capacities.name: Technique
capacities.description: Produce the intended stroke and contact.

capacities.name: Athleticism
capacities.description: Reach balls from different positions and place the shot where intended while retaining the technique.

capacities.name: Intellect
capacities.description: Combine the shots you can actually play into patterns.

capacities.name: Reading
capacities.description: Choose and adapt patterns for the opponent and situation across this point, match and later encounters.

loop: Play and notice where the point fails.
Name the Current Most Limiting Factor (CMLF): the capacity that may be limiting the intended result right now.
Predict what a focused practice change should alter.
Try it, then return to a point and check.
If the same problem remains, revise the diagnosis.
prompt: Before the adjustment: what do you expect to change, and what would count as evidence?

scenarios.label: Movement
scenarios.description: The ball follows the same path. Change where the player stands and how far they reach. Check whether the racket meets the ball at its fixed contact point.

scenarios.label: Technique
scenarios.description: The ball follows a manageable feed. Keep the player in place and change swing timing. Compare racket and ball at contact.

scenarios.label: Reading
scenarios.description: Follow the three connected shots in this exchange. Move the opponent while keeping the ball path the same, then compare which shots still fit that position.

examples.title: Movement comparison
examples.description: At the fixed contact moment, the player begins short of the ball. Move to the contact position and see whether the displayed separation changes.

examples.title: Technique comparison
examples.description: On a manageable feed, compare the intended stroke and contact. A miss during a point does not diagnose this cause by itself.

feedback.separation: The gap shows how far the racket is from the ball at the selected moment. To tell whether the player arrived late, you also need to see how they moved.

readingCopy: A pattern can help you win this point and also teach an opponent what to expect next time. Reading includes both. Keeping a tactic hidden is not automatically worth more than winning the point you are playing. Weigh what you get now against what the other person learns for later.
